name: Support Ticket Dashboard
summary: Support staff can quickly find tickets, understand priority, and see the current open-ticket workload.
primaryJourneys: Open the dashboard and see the open-ticket workload.
Filter tickets by status or priority.
Search for tickets by customer name.
outcomes: The dashboard displays tickets in a table with customer name, status, and priority visible.
Changing the status filter updates the table to show only matching tickets.
Changing the priority filter updates the table to show only matching tickets.
Entering a customer name search updates the table to matching tickets.
The dashboard shows a count equal to the currently open tickets.
The dashboard builds successfully for deployment.
dataConcepts: Ticket with customer name, status, and priority
observations: The request centers on rapid queue inspection rather than ticket management.
Status, priority, and customer search are the primary retrieval dimensions.

designDirection.reason: The requested behaviors are all fastest to use in one operational table.
designDirection.layoutApproach: Wide table with a compact summary row and controls above it.
designDirection.mobilePriority: Collapse ticket columns into stacked rows while keeping filters prominent.
accessibilityConsiderations: Use labeled controls and visible focus states.
Do not rely on color alone for status or priority.

creativeDNA.thesis: Treat ticket discovery as a high-speed retrieval tool.
creativeDNA.audienceResponse: Feel fast and focused while narrowing the queue.

includedDefaults: Show the open-ticket count for the current filtered result set while labeling it clearly.
Preserve active filters and search text when the visible ticket list refreshes.
Add sortable columns for status, priority, and customer name.
constraints: No ticket creation, editing, deletion, assignment, or reply workflow is included.
No authentication, external ticket integration, or customer-facing portal is included.
Use a responsive table-first dashboard with client-side filtering and search for the requested ticket list.
assumptions: Ticket data is available as representative dashboard content because no source system or records were supplied.
Open tickets include every ticket whose status is not closed.
architectureDecisions: Use a responsive table-first dashboard with client-side filtering and search for the requested ticket list.
